We emit the right two directory values under two key names the page never mentions, and neither documented key exists anywhere in the tree.

• Sole producer: packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:163-174. The `pi.on('user_bash', ...)` handler compares the reported cwd against `lastCwd` and, on a delta only, emits at :168-172 `{ hook_event_name: 'CwdChanged', cwd, ...(previous ? { previous_cwd: previous } : {}) }`. `cwd` (:170) is the NEW directory; `previous` (:166) is the old one.
• Type: packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:800-802 — under the comment `// Working-directory change events`, `SdkAutomationInput` declares `cwd?: string;` and `previous_cwd?: string;` and nothing else for this event.

That array is declarative inventory, not a runtime filter: its only readers are `PI_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_CONTRACTS` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:25) and `getAgentEventContractV1` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:217).

divergence: Values right, key names wrong — that is the whole delta, and it changes the fix from "produce missing data" to "add two aliases". `new_cwd` is a pure alias of a value we already ship: our common `cwd` holds the new directory, which is precisely what the doc's own example puts in `cwd` (cwd == new_cwd there). `old_cwd` is data we do carry but under the non-contract name `previous_cwd`. Everything else about the event already conforms: it fires once per directory change (packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:165, delta-guarded), it is matcher-less (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:359-361 `MATCHER_IGNORED_AGENT_EVENTS`), and it carries no decision control (contract row `kind: 'observational'`, packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:72). NOT part of this row, though specified on the same page for the same event: `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` access (hooks.md:2433 — docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-hook-context-injection.md:302 already records that our CwdChanged hooks' env writes are never read) and the `watchPaths` output field (hooks.md:2454-2458).

change.what: Two added keys, additive only. Emit `new_cwd: cwd` unconditionally and `old_cwd: previous` in the same conditional spread that already sets `previous_cwd`, keeping both existing keys: `await options.emit('CwdChanged', { hook_event_name: 'CwdChanged', cwd, new_cwd: cwd, ...(previous ? { previous_cwd: previous, old_cwd: previous } : {}) })`. Do NOT rename `previous_cwd` away — keep it as a permanent read-path alias the way packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts keeps legacy permission-mode spellings and format-adapters.ts:149 keeps the Elicitation alias, because stored native automations and existing hook scripts were authored against it.

change.symbol: SdkAutomationInput, the `// Working-directory change events` block (lines 800-802)
change.what: Add `old_cwd?: string;` and `new_cwd?: string;` beside the existing `cwd?`/`previous_cwd?`, with a doc comment quoting hooks.md § CwdChanged input and stating that `new_cwd` mirrors the common `cwd` and `previous_cwd` is the retained legacy alias of `old_cwd`. This is the type both the subprocess and the host import, so one edit covers both ends of the wire.

Change `redactedPayload: ['cwd', 'previous_cwd']` to `redactedPayload: ['cwd', 'new_cwd', 'old_cwd', 'previous_cwd']`. One array literal. This row is the documentation-of-record consumed by PI_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_CONTRACTS and getAgentEventContractV1; it does not gate or strip the payload at runtime, so this edit alone changes no behaviour — it just stops the frozen inventory from disagreeing with the emitter.

`expect(emitted[0]?.input).toEqual({ hook_event_name: 'CwdChanged', cwd: '/repo/sub' })` is exact-equality and WILL fail on the added keys — update it to `{ hook_event_name: 'CwdChanged', cwd: '/repo/sub', new_cwd: '/repo/sub' }`. Also add a third `user_bash` with a different cwd (e.g. '/repo/other') and assert that emission carries `old_cwd: '/repo/sub'` and `previous_cwd: '/repo/sub'`: today's fixture (lines 70-71) only ever exercises the first-cwd branch, so the old-directory keys would otherwise ship untested.

userImpact: Silent wrong output for one concrete population: a user installs a Claude plugin whose CwdChanged hook reads the documented field — the direnv-style recipe the page itself motivates, e.g. `new=$(cat | jq -r '.new_cwd')`. Today the hook registers, fires on every `cd`, and exits 0, so Sources shows it healthy and the automations run log shows a successful run with no stderr. But `jq` yields `null`, so the environment reload the plugin exists to perform either does nothing or acts on the literal string "null", and the user's per-directory toolchain silently never activates. Same for `.old_cwd` in any hook that diffs the two directories. Nothing tells them why. A native Nessy automation authored against our own field names is unaffected, and users with no Claude CwdChanged plugin see nothing at all — so the blast is narrow, but where it lands it is invisible rather than loud, which is the worse failure mode.

One deliberate design call the implementer should not silently reverse: keeping `previous_cwd` alongside the new `old_cwd`. Removing it would be a breaking change for any native automation or hook script written against today's shape, and this repo's convention (mode-types.ts permission aliases, format-adapters.ts:149 Elicitation alias) is that read-path aliases are permanent.
